title: The Characteristics of Kingdom Ambassadors
paragraphs: In fact, we will talk about understanding the original mission and the role of this thing we call the Church. I think one of the saddest things that happened in the church is that the church turned into a mere witness. You know, if you are a professional communicator but your information is wrong, then you are successful in spreading intellectual pollution. You know, there's nothing worse than an effective communicator who conveys the wrong ideas.

One of the most important phrases I found in the Bible that shocked me is found in the Gospel of Matthew, chapter ten. In chapter 10, Jesus spoke words to his disciples and told them to go out and share some information with people. But before they go, the text says that he sent them with these instructions. He not only sent them, but he guided them first. Ah, his first instructions were shocking. I will quote it for you. Don't go. Now if you don't believe me, read the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 10 immediately.

You will find those instructions directed to the students. He said, “Do not go to the nations, but go only to the house of Israel.” Imagine that he sends them to preach the good news of the kingdom, but he tells them where not to go. How can a teaching from God be negative when it comes to sharing good news? Because he knew that their attitude towards nations would not serve the message. They were biased.

He knew that they would therefore distort the concepts to suit their bias, and end up conveying a false message, which is of course embodied in the Book of Acts when they tried to make the nations follow the traditions of Judaism, and it became a corrupt message. My point is this. We have learned so well that facts have become so corrupted that when we are confronted with the truth, we consider it to be wrong. I have been suffering from this myself. Therefore, I want to talk about this aspect of the Kingdom of God.

I want to talk about representation in the Kingdom. But from my point of view... let me present the idea first. Let's talk about the foreign affairs of the Kingdom. Every kingdom is a government. I will make some observations here. This is found in the Book of Isaiah, chapter nine. In fact, this is the part of the chapter and verse that we really overlook. We like the rest of the verse. In Isaiah, chapter 9, verse 6, it says: “ For to us a child is born, to us a son is given.” We know this part.

But the following phrase says: "And the presidency rests on his shoulders." Now, the first statement made about this Christ is that of a government. He is coming to Earth carrying something on his shoulders. In Isaiah’s days, it was a common practice for a person to carry a yoke on his shoulder to carry his master’s belongings. So in Isaiah's days, yoke was made for both humans and animals. They still do that in the Far East today. In Eastern countries, the yoke was common for both men and women.

The servant was wearing a yoke. They would carve a yoke the size of your neck with two ends like a piece of wood. And you would carry buckets to transport your master's loads. Whether it was water, wheat, rocks, or whatever you were carrying, you were carrying loads on your shoulders and around your neck. This is the same concept that Isaiah talks about when he refers to the coming of the Messiah. He says, "For to us a child is born, to us a son is given." Now the following phrase means two things.

First, he will be a servant. Only the servants carry the yoke. And what will be on his shoulder? What? the government. So he is coming with something on his shoulders. It is a government. So, two things about him. Firstly, he is a servant. Secondly, he holds a government for someone else. Servants never carry loads for themselves. Rather, they always carry burdens for other people, for their masters in most cases.

In this case, the image you should draw in your mind is that Jesus, the Messiah, comes to earth as a servant carrying someone’s possessions on his shoulders, and he is coming to return them to their owners. Can you picture that image in your mind? So he comes to Earth as a servant, and what does he bring? A government on his shoulders. This is what he brought. He did not bring any debt. He did not bring traditions. He didn't even come for prayer meetings. But what did he bring? With a government.

Now, please note that if you read that verse carefully, it does not say "governments" in the plural. It refers to a single government, a specific kingdom. The presidency rests on his shoulders, meaning that God truly intended only one government on Earth from the beginning, and in the end, He will achieve it. There are many governments on Earth today, but God only has one in mind. He explains what it is in the following statement. He says, " And his kingdom will last for what? Forever.

He will reign over his kingdom forever. So, what did he bring? A government that is a kingdom. That's why Jesus' first public declaration is in Matthew 4:17. His first public declaration says this: 'From that time Jesus began to preach what? The kingdom of heaven is at hand.' His introduction was about a kingdom, about a government. That's what he brought. Why is this so important? Because as long as it's just religion, you'll never understand the message. I'm trying so hard to get out of religion.

I'm really trying. I mean, it's hard for me. I'm trying to get rid of religion in my life because religion is holding me back. Religion is man's search for God. It's man's attempt to find God, to reach God. That's religion. That's why religion is full of activities and rituals and all sorts of traditions because we're trying to please the gods. And in the Christian religious conception, the Christian is God, but it's the same thing. We're trying to connect with God, to reach God. But this message is different.

First, this message is that God is reaching out to us. He sent his only Son. We don't need to reach out." To him. And secondly, he didn't bring rituals. He brought authority. He brought power. He brought the power of the Kingdom. He brought you the ability to control your environment again. He brought you the power to take responsibility for your circumstances again. He restored to Earth the authority to govern the planet again. That's what he brought. What did he bring? Government.

So, the Kingdom is the influence of a ruler and the structure of a king over a territory. Now, the second point is important. The Kingdom is the influence of a ruler. Everything Jesus taught was Kingdom. Jesus never taught a religion. He taught Kingdom. And he kept emphasizing this message that the Kingdom had come. The Kingdom is like, the Kingdom is like, the Kingdom is like. And he tried so hard to convince us that he kept using what are called parables. Parables.

And in each parable, he was trying to simplify things for people. To the farmer, he said the Kingdom of God is like a seed. To the fisherman, he said the Kingdom of God is like a man casting a net. To the businessman, he said the Kingdom of God is like a man investing in a faraway country. I mean, he kept using them. He said, "Look, this message has to get to the housewife." He says, "The Kingdom of God is like a woman who was searching "About a pearl, or a coin you lost." He kept repeating this even to the farmer.

He says, "The kingdom of God is like a man working in a field." He says, "This message must reach everyone." He says, "What is the depth of this kingdom?" “When you discover the truth about the Kingdom, it sets you free.” What is the Kingdom? Structure and influence. Every government establishes a system of foreign relations to represent its interests. Isn’t that right? Now remember that the Kingdom of God is a government. Every government in the world establishes a structure for its foreign relations.

The purpose of foreign relations is to advance your interests on the international stage. That’s why governments have foreign ministries. In fact, let me move on to the next point. I’ll help you understand that the structure is called “ foreign missions.” Does that sound familiar? Foreign mission. The word is singular. Foreign mission. When I visited England years ago and they took me to the Embassy of the Bahamas, the word on the door wasn’t “Embassy,” it was “Bahamian Mission.”

Did you know that in every country, if you read the documents relating to an embassy or an ambassador, you’ll find it’s called a mission? So, we have countries in the Caribbean with foreign mission offices around the world. Why are they there? They’re there to represent our government. Now, what do they call it in the United States? The Department of State. The Department of State is a department headed by the chief ambassador, who happens to be… Colin Powell. Colin Powell is the chief U. S. ambassador.

They have dozens of ambassadors around the world from America, but he's the chief. He represents the State Department. Everyone, the State Department. That's what the United States calls it. The British, whose culture we inherited, we call it a mission, the Department of Foreign Missions. Interesting words. You religious people, not you, but the person sitting next to you, the one I'm talking to. You say, "Let's go on missions," right? We say that Jesus's words, the last words of Christ, were what? A great mission.

So, we're here, in parentheses, on a mission. Well, only foreign officials have missions. Governments set up missions in countries to influence those countries with their policies. And they're there to advance and protect their interests in that country. It's called a mission, a foreign mission. The State Department. Okay, what kind of work do they do? It's called foreign affairs. The person in charge of our mission, our chief mission, pay attention to this.

Our chief missionary is the person in charge of the State Department. Colin Powell, you might be watching this program somewhere. In your office. You are a chief missionary. You represent a government called the Federal Government of the United States, and your job is to be the chief missionary for your government. So when there are problems in the Middle East or Croatia or India, they send the chief missionary to express the government's thoughts on the situation. Is anyone following me?

Can I simplify this quickly? When you go to your job tomorrow, it means that Heaven has just sent a chief missionary to that position. And your job is to provide Heaven's perspective on the entire environment and the circumstances you find there. Chief missionary. So all ambassadors are missionaries. Their job is not to represent themselves. They are there to represent their government. Therefore, ambassadors are charged with this duty of representing their government. Take note of this point.

An ambassador is charged with the duty of representing their government. It is very important. An ambassador's responsibility is never to represent themselves. They represent the government of the country they belong to. That is the duty of an ambassador. I want to take you on a quick tour through the Bible to talk a little bit about the church. Then why did this thing called a church become necessary?

We learned in our last session that the word " church" which Jesus used it in Matthew chapter 16, and it's a powerful phrase: the word "ecclesia." He said, " I will build my church (ecclesia ) on the fact that I am the Christ." The word ecclesia means the called, the chosen, the appointed. And the word ecclesia isn't a word Jesus invented. The Greeks literally invented the word ecclesia. They were the first to coin the word "ecclesia," which the Romans adopted in their government when they conquered Greece.

The Romans dominated the world and enjoyed success for 200 years. They ruled the entire world. The Roman Empire, and one of the main forces that enabled them to do this, was their governmental structure. The government of Rome was the first empire to build a structure similar to, or identical with, the structure of the Kingdom of God. That's why Christ came during the Roman era, so that the terminology could be understood. No other empire ruled the way the Romans did. Caesar lived in Rome, yet he ran the world.

He made the whole world like Rome. In fact, the phrase we coined is, "When in Rome, do as the Romans do." In other words, whenever you entered Roman territory, you had to act like a Roman, think like a Roman, dress like a Roman, and eat like a Roman because you were now in Roman territory. This didn't mean you went to Rome. It meant that wherever his influence reached, it became just like Rome. Caesar achieved this. That's why the Bible says, " In the fullness of time, God sent his Son."

Fullness means the right time and the right circumstances. He sent Christ. He came himself. God himself came at the time when an empire was established that was exactly like his kingdom. Even when he uses terminology, it's by definition. So Jesus couldn't say, "On this rock I will build the church." He couldn't say that because there were other churches already. The Romans had their own church. Caesar had his church. He called it that, and it was his Senate. Today we call that the Cabinet.

Ah, Caesar's Senate was his Cabinet. Today, your Cabinet is n't the ministers in the House of Representatives or the members of Congress. Those aren't Cabinet ministers. They're just representatives of constituencies. Are you following me? Members of Parliament and Congress are representatives of the people. But the Cabinet is different. The Cabinet is appointed by the Prime Minister, the President, or the King. They are appointed personally by him without consulting anyone. That group is called the Ecclesia.

There is a statement Jesus made that we still don't understand unless we understand government. It was a political statement. Would you like to hear it? Many are invited. Many people are elected to the House of Representatives, but only a few are appointed to the Cabinet. You never elect a Cabinet minister. The Cabinet minister is chosen by the King, the President, or the Prime Minister. Are you ready for this? The same power of choice is given to ambassadors. Ambassadors are never elected.

Your opinion counts nothing. This is a decision of the leader of the nation. He chooses the ambassadors of his own free will. This is the Church of the Ecclesia. Christ says, "As the Christ, the Son of the living God, I will choose my reign based on my being King." I am the Lord. I am God in the flesh. I am the Christ. Therefore, I can choose my government. Guess who he chose? "He's sitting next to someone. Let me tell you why I'm so happy. And soon, you'll understand why this is so important.

But, if we had to vote for you to enter the kingdom, you would never have arrived. There are many people who are saddened by your salvation. They ca n't believe that God is using you. They know a lot about your history and your past. They know who you ate with, slept with, drank with, and who you used drugs with. They know you very well. They say that you can never amount to anything. And God says, 'Oh really?'" " I chose them." You all better thank God that you did n't vote for yourselves to enter this kingdom.

Praise be to God. Will you shout a little more? Let's say, " Thank God for that." Some of you have a past no one knows about, but thank God, He overlooks your flaws and makes you part of His own circle. Glory to God. Imagine God telling Paul secrets after Paul had been killing Christians. You would never have voted for Paul to enter God's government. Never. He was a murderer. Yet, God gave him information that even Peter didn't receive. Paul says, " The vision I have is very great."

I thank God that no one voted for me to enter. Praise be to God. I say, "Thank God that no one voted for me to enter this kingdom." Praise be to God.” That was the king’s choice. So, the church’s mission is to represent God’s government and act as ambassadors for heaven. What is our job? To recruit citizens for God’s kingdom. Later in this series, we’ll talk about what that means—recruiting citizens. But let me just say for now that we’re not really recruiting new citizens. Okay.

The only way to describe this, I think, to help you understand, is to use an analogy. Ah… let’s say we were fighting in a war and… while we were fighting in the war, the generals got together and made a deal and the war was over, but we were still in the jungle and didn’t know. So we were fighting each other and killing each other in the jungle while the war was over. We hadn’t gotten the message yet.

Then they sent people to all the places in the jungle where we were still fighting to bring us the good news that the war was over. That’s how it is. So our job is to go into the jungle of the world and tell people that the war is over. He has won. There’s no need to fight anymore. The battle is over. You can have peace with God. Again, Ephesians 3:10 tells us a little about this work. It says, "His intention was that through the church, the manifold wisdom of God would be made known to whom?"

" To the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms, according to His eternal purpose. His original purpose was that, through His government, He would reveal His manifold wisdom. Are you wise enough to understand that verse? Look at the verse again. It's an interesting verse. 'Purpose' means ' original purpose.' His original purpose was what? Through the church. Where is the church? Now I see that I know where your mind just went.

Your mind immediately went to a building with pews, stained-glass windows, some choirs, and all that. Look, the word ' church' is jumbled in your mind right now. I know that the word ' church' means a religious organization with lots of candles, lots of songs, traditions, hymn books, and prayer meetings. That's the church. But that's not what it means. What does it mean? A cabinet. A government cabinet. A select group of people to represent the prime minister's thoughts.

Read it now, and you'll see that it makes sense. His original purpose was that, through His cabinet, God's manifold, or multifaceted, wisdom would be revealed, to become what? A phenomenon. He wanted to show His nature through His cabinet. You're looking at me in surprise. Am I speaking in an incomprehensible language? Does what I'm saying make sense? Let me give you an example. The cabinet doesn't represent the people. Oh, think about it. The cabinet of any country doesn't represent the people.

Members of parliament represent the people. Members of Congress, but not the cabinet. The cabinet represents the person who chose them. It's a slightly different way of thinking. That's why, when you're appointed to the cabinet, they immediately put you under a law called collective responsibility. This law means that once you become a member of the government, you can no longer express your personal opinion. Now, some of you will realize this after I'm gone. It's true. This is what Jesus is talking about.

A minister in the government cannot express his own opinion. That's why you get kicked out of the government. When you express your opinion, you are no longer loyal to the person who appointed you. God says, "I have chosen my people." Why? So that they can demonstrate my will on earth, so that the angels can see. The only thing that works tomorrow is his mind, his attitude, his response to life. That's why, as a believer— listen carefully, look at me now—you should never use that term again.

I'll give you peace of mind. Because as a believer in the kingdom of God, you don't have a mind. To calm him down, do you understand? In our government, in the previous administration, two cabinet ministers expressed their personal opinions. What happened? They were fired immediately. There was no room for discussion. And this happens in every government everywhere—in the United States, in Jamaica, in Barbados.

If you disagree with the prime minister or the president in the government, if you disagree, you're fired. You know, some of you looked at Clinton years ago, and of course, most of us realized that Clinton was guilty. Most of us figured it out. But when he met with the press, remember that time he came out of the White House, the microphones were there, and behind him was his cabinet, and he spoke, and they were all standing there. They knew, but they couldn't disagree. They had to speak carefully about it.

Make it sound like it was just what? A collective responsibility. In other words, if someone asks you about homosexuality, you don't give your personal opinion. You give the king's opinion. You don't adapt to the environment. You adopt his words and tell them, " That's what the prime minister says." Come on, someone say amen. But we're not ready. For the life of the kingdom. As you can see, we're so democratic that we discuss everything. Christ says adultery is a sin.

Well, you know, Lord, you don't understand how difficult it is. You know, you know, Lord, you know he's handsome. She's beautiful, Lord. I mean, Lord, if you saw what you saw, what do you mean by what you saw? What are you talking about? You don't discuss things with the king. But as you can see, we're still Christians. We're not citizens. We're elders, not ambassadors. Our minds need refreshing. Let's look at this other point here. I thought it was interesting. What is the ministry of the ecclesiastical office?

The church. The church as an institution doesn't go into the world first as an institution, but exists to train saints to go themselves. Is that right? Yes. The pastor of the church in God's government temple is considered your chief attaché. He will be considered your chief ambassador in that region. So, in this diplomatic center where the diplomats are meeting today, I will be considered the chief diplomat. Is that clear? Or you can call me the foreign minister of this particular local community. Is that clear?

I am the foreign minister. Now, My job is to train you to go back to your local areas to be ambassadors in your jobs, in your homes, in your communities, and to train you to influence those areas for the benefit of the government. That's what I'm here for. So, what we do now is meet at the embassy, ​​which is called the Diplomatic Center. We meet as diplomats. That's what an ambassador does— the work of diplomacy.

And we're here to discuss our government's constitution to get the mind of our King, so that we can go out and properly represent the Kingdom of Heaven. That's what we meet for every week. We don't just meet for excitement. We meet to do government business. Can we get that in our heads? So when someone asks you again where you're going, tell them I'm going to the embassy to get instructions on the constitution. If you say "church," it goes back to the idea of ​​pews and pulpits.

You come for the excitement instead of the transformation. When you become an ambassador appointed by the government, do you know what they do? They put you through a training program, an intensive training program. The first thing you have to learn, guess what? The name of every country. You know, there are people who didn't know That there was a country called Croatia or Afghanistan until problems arose there. So, the first thing an ambassador must learn is his world.

Paul says, "Do not be ignorant of the devil's schemes." His thoughts. Study your enemy. Discover your lands. Discover your whole world. This is yours. You know, man, shepherd, it's amazing how I've begun to change. I used to love Abraham's blessing until I met Jesus. Abraham was never promised the whole planet. You'll get it after I'm gone. Abraham was promised a small piece of land. Well, that's good. Thank God for that. Is that what you want? Okay.

But look, I used to enjoy Abraham's blessings until I realized they were limited. And I decided I wanted Adam's blessing. The first, original blessing. Come on, talk to me. God took man and put him in the Garden and said, " Rule over all the earth." "It's not just the piece of land they're fighting over right now. Yes, sir. You'll get it after I'm gone. Yes, sir. So, if you're an ambassador, you need to get to know the whole place. I decided before I died that I would visit every country.

When I understood this, I started moving. I'm moving. I'm moving. I'm moving, man. I'm moving. I'm moving. Thank God. Look, nothing ever happens until you start believing in it. Some of you think your territory is just Miami. So, you never go beyond Miami. You go shopping. Thank God. Some of you go a little further. You get to Orlando. Wow! Glory. West Palm Beach. Wow! I'm really moving now. I'm still in Florida.

But if you start thinking that China is my territory, and Haiti is my territory, and Canada, God will start opening doors for you. The kingdom works by faith, by belief. If you don't believe that something belongs to you, it will never come to you. It never will. That's why the church is here to train you to go all over the world. Ephesians 4:10 says this. He himself gave some To be apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers— to do what? To train saints to do what? To perform ministry.

So that they may mature and be built in the image of Christ. Therefore, the job of a local embassy is to train diplomats to perform what more effectively? Ministry. In the Bahamas, all government agencies are called ministries. In Jamaica, they are called ministries. In Barbados, they are called ministries. But in the church, they are called ministries. Ministry is not just a religious word. My God. Our education department is called the Ministry of Education. Why? That's what they serve.

Our health department is called the Ministry of Health. Why? They are all servants, and they are in the service of healing. So, the next time someone asks you, " Should a Christian be involved in politics?" "Your answer should be: It's too late. Clap, folks. That's a good way to clap. It's too late. I'm already involved. I'm the biggest politician you've ever seen. And I don't represent any people. I represent an entire government from somewhere else. That's what we missed.

We missed the concepts, and that's why we're fighting. You'll see, once you become a religion, you become part of other religions, and they become your rivals. You just heard something important. Please buy this tape. I'll say it again. If you reduce this to a religion, you become one of the religions fighting for souls. And so your enemies become people like the followers of Islam, Buddhism, Shintoism, Taoism, Confucianism, the Baha'i Faith, and you start to see these people as your enemies.

They are not your enemies. God never called Abraham to a religion, but his descendants turned it into one. And by the time it appeared, the religion was so powerful that it became more important than the word of God. So what did they do?" With their religion? They turned their religion against the Gentiles ( non-Jews). The Gentiles became their enemies. They turned their religion against the pagans. By the way, paganism is a religion. It's not against Christ. Pagans are religious people.

The Romans were worshippers. They worshipped many gods. The Greeks were worshippers. They were pagans. Pagan gods are gods. That's what they worship. There are many gods. So, paganism isn't a non-religious word. It's a description of a religion. And the Jews, the Judaizers, hated the pagans. That's why they couldn't eat with people or talk to people. Why? They made people their enemies. It sounds familiar. Some of you hate others. You hate Muslims. You hate Buddhists. What? They're not like us.

You've turned everything into a religion. So you've created enemies who don't exist. Who are these people? I'll tell you who they are. Christ said who they are. He says, "Oh, your brother who was once lost." Go and get it from the sheep pen. He is your brother. These are the family. They are a distorted image of God. Your perception of a person determines how you treat them. This is correct. This is correct. I mean, you don't engage with or talk to an enemy, do you?

So, when you see a woman walking around with her face covered by a large headscarf and wearing a long dress, your first thought is: I'm going to cross to the other side of the road. Why? We do not deal with the Samaritans. This sounds familiar. However, here is Jesus walking to the same well, sitting down by it, and asking it for water. Imagine asking a Muslim for food. Let's have lunch together. Oh. Oh no. My Christianity is so weak that it might be tainted by your Islamic beliefs. Muslims are human beings.

Buddhists are human beings. Rastafarians are human beings. Hindus are human beings. They are searching, just like all of us, trying to find God. The only difference is that you found it. No, it is He who found you. Hallelujah. I say Hallelujah. Your task is to introduce him to them. He is a God of love. The church has made itself a religion. Now we are in a state of competition. You know, when a mosque is built, I feel excited because I see, you know, that the future of that place has already been decided.

So there's no problem with that. I care about the people inside it. Not one stone will be left upon another. And this whole thing will end. So don't worry about the buildings. It is people's hearts that need to be pursued, loved, forgiven, and have your heart opened to them. I mean, every sinner Jesus met became his friend. He used to sit with drunkards and prostitutes. He was called the friend of sinners. What kind of man is this? Because he is chasing after people. He did not seek out converts to his religion.

It will reach you someday. Let's talk briefly about the representation of the Kingdom. Ephesians 6:19 says, “ Look at this.” Please write this down. Paul now understands the meaning of the kingdom. He says: “ Pray also for me, that words may be given to me when I open my mouth, so that I may proclaim the mystery of the gospel.” The word Gospel here refers to only one message, which is the Kingdom of God. The Kingdom of God. Now the next phrase.

For the sake of this gospel, the kingdom of God, I am an ambassador in chains. So pray for me that I may proclaim this good news with the boldness I ought to have. Paul says, "Look, I'm an ambassador, and I'm in chains by the government. I'm a prisoner of the good news. I'm bound by loyalty to my King. I'm bound by my responsibility to the government. I'm bound. When you become a cabinet minister, you're a prisoner. A prisoner of whom? A prisoner of the government. Can I suggest something?

Ah, that doesn't happen, of course. I mean, it might, but you won't win, I'll just say this. All governments argue, but you never know about those disagreements. Behind closed doors, when President Bush meets with his cabinet, they trade harsh accusations. They disagree and they shout and all. But when they settle on a decision and the president makes his final decision, everyone comes out and says the same thing. All governments go through periods where they need to make up their minds.

They have to argue to the end. They have to put their minds to it and work together, but not in public. It's never known to the public. Do you all hear me? When they come out of that room, there's only one statement they make: ' My government says.' You know, something I've noticed about this government that We call it the church. Sit properly before we go. Come on. We go in here, chat quickly about what's happening, and then go out and tell everyone what happened inside. Why? You're religious.

You're not the government. When an unbeliever attacks one of your brothers, you're supposed to defend him, not join that person. Ah, but we're not there yet. We're not mature enough to be like Christ. Look at how Jesus operated. Watch this. He was a brilliant politician. Watch him at work. The Bible says that he stood before the crowds every time and spoke in parables. Then the Bible says, " And when they were alone, in the government meeting, he explained to them everything he had said." Yes, sir.

They were so annoyed by his political vision that they once asked him, " Leader, why do you always speak to them in parables, while you speak to us plainly?" He said, “So that they may see and not see, and hear and not understand.” You have been given the knowledge of the mystery. Look, let me tell you something, my friends. When you come into the body of Christ, our affairs are secret. We know that you are sinning. We know that you are not living the right way, but we are not required to announce it to everyone.

Say “Amen” aloud. Anyway, some of you have begun to keep quiet. You know that things are happening in the body of Christ, but you are not going to spread them around the world. Hallelujah. Go ahead. God used to dismiss people, and they didn't even realize they were being dismissed. He would always call his followers aside and tell them profound things. Then he would tell them, “Don't tell anyone about this.” Look, you don't understand the mentality of a cabinet. We are supposed to protect one another.

That's why a prime minister or a president feels betrayed when a minister speaks against him. Because that minister is supposed to protect him. How do you think Jesus feels when he tells people who he is, and then you go and act in the opposite way? Disappointed. You ask everyone That they do what is right while you do not. Jesus wants us to understand this embassy responsibility. Loyalty to your government. Paul says, "What am I? I am bound by my government. I am bound by the Cabinet.

I can no longer go where I want, or do what I want, or eat what I want, or drink what I want. I must abide by the law of the government. I used to go to nightclubs, spend the nights, have fun, drink, and do all that. I used to, but now I am bound by another government." You can say Amen before I wrap up this morning. Okay, say Amen.
